title: Collections: Working with Javascript Arrays
summary: Introduces arrays as a way to keep many related values in one variable, covering literal syntax, zero-based indexing, length and includes(). Exercise: a birthday-party guest list checker.

concepts.heading: Why arrays
points: A variable so far held one value. Checking a name against many names with a long chain of if/else if would be unmanageable.
An array is an ordered collection of related items stored in one variable (an egg box compared with a single egg).

concepts.heading: Syntax and indexing
points: Create with square brackets and comma-separated items: var eggs = [item0, item1, ...].
Read an item with name[position]. Square brackets both create and access arrays, a hint that you are dealing with a collection.
Positions start at 0, so eggs[1] is the second item and guestList[0] the first.
array.length returns the number of items. Logging the whole array in the console also shows its size.
Strings in the array need quotes.

concepts.heading: includes()
points: array.includes(value) searches the array and returns true if any element matches, otherwise false.
The boolean result is directly usable as an if condition.
(Extra) Matching is strict and case-sensitive: "angela" does not match "Angela".

code_examples.caption: Array basics
code_examples.code:
var guestList = ["Wesley", "Maria", "Michele", "Eveline", "Levi", "Everaldo"];
console.log(guestList);         // whole array
console.log(guestList.length);  // 6
console.log(guestList[0]);      // "Wesley"
console.log(guestList.includes("Maria"));   // true

task.name: Birthday party guest list
task.starting_point: Empty script with an array of guest names.
task.goal: Ask for the visitor's name and check the guest list.
steps: Create the guestList array of strings.
Store the answer of prompt("What is your name?") in a variable such as guestName.
Use guestList.includes(guestName) as the if condition.
Alert a welcome message when true; alert a polite refusal in the else branch.
Test with a listed name and a random one.
task.expected_result: Names on the list get a welcome alert; any other input gets the refusal alert.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 15 - Intermediate Javascript/15.07 -  Collections - Working with Javascript Arrays/script.js

pitfalls: Forgetting commas or quotes in the array literal.
Case or whitespace differences making includes() return false.
Reference repo includes an author footer in index.html that should be ignored.

playground.coverage: Covers array creation, indexing, last item, length, includes, indexOf and the doorman prompt example, plus const behaviour.
